reference.title: Cascade reference
reference.shortdesc: The Default column lists values used by CSSMedia’s current PDF-oriented rule evaluation. Media-query width, height and ratio values use the A4 default page size.

ul.li: ? means optional, | means choose one, # means one or more comma-separated items, || means one or more options in any order, and brackets group parts of the syntax.
<label> is an encoding name.
<url-or-string> and <string-or-url> each mean a URL or quoted string.
<namespace-prefix> is the prefix bound to a namespace.
<layer-name> names a cascade layer. <layer-name-list> is a comma-separated list of layer names.
<stylesheet> is a CSS stylesheet.
<custom-property-name> is a custom property name beginning with --.
<declaration-list> is a list of declarations.
<block-contents> is content inside a rule’s braces, including declarations and nested rules.

<declaration-value> is the value part of a declaration: one or more CSS tokens, such as navy, calc(1em + 2px) or var(--size). It cannot contain a top-level semicolon or !, since those delimit declarations and !important. Semicolons and exclamation marks inside functions are not top-level. See CSS Syntax 3.
<string> is a quoted CSS string.
<media-query-list> is one or more comma-separated media queries.
<rule-list> is a sequence of rules.
<condition> and <supports-condition> are support conditions made from feature tests and boolean operators.
<supports-condition-name> names a reusable support condition.
<container-condition> optionally names a query container and gives its query.
<boolean-condition> combines media() and supports() tests.
<scope-start> and <scope-end> are selector lists that set the scope roots and limits of @scope.
<extension-name> names a custom media query.
<name> in the function syntax is a function name beginning with --.
<parameters> is a comma-separated list of function parameters.
<type> is the optional syntax expected for the function result.
<declaration-rule-list> contains declarations and nested rules.
<number> in the function example is a CSS number, which can be an integer or include a fractional part.

section.p: The @charset rule must be the first rule in a stylesheet to affect byte decoding. Use @namespace before ordinary rules, and place @import rules before namespace declarations and ordinary rules.
Function names start with --. Parameters can have a syntax type and a default value. Use the result descriptor for the returned value:

@supports declaration tests use parentheses. selector() tests one complex selector. font-tech(), font-format() and at-rule() test supported features. A named condition is tested by placing its name inside parentheses:
@when conditions combine media() and supports() tests with and, or and not. Parentheses group mixed operators:
Use @else immediately after an @when, @media, @supports or @container branch. An unrelated rule ends the chain.

section.title: Media features
section.p: Media feature values describe the page or PDF environment used for conditional rule evaluation. They do not describe a screen.

ul.li: <ratio> is a ratio of two numbers.
<integer> is a whole number.
<length> is a CSS length, such as 12pt or 2em.
<mq-boolean> is an integer with the value 0 or 1.
<resolution> is a pixel density, such as 300dpi.

section.title: Container size features
section.p: A size query in @container tests the size of the nearest ancestor that has container-type. An ancestor with size answers all these features, and an ancestor with inline-size answers only the features of the inline axis.

section.title: Container style queries
section.p: A container style query uses style() to test a computed style or custom property on an ancestor. See Conditional rules.
